baseline.rationale: gpt-5-6-luna is DEFAULT_MODEL_ID -- the fixed path every request takes today, and therefore the thing Auto has to beat to justify replacing it. gpt-5-4-mini is the baseline for the separate question of changing that default, not for ROUTE-01.

judge.rationale: mposition's choice. It is also the baseline, so it grades its own answer in every pair -- the baseline arm is gpt-5-6-luna on all 210. That is the self-preference docs/ops/tomverse-chat-router-evaluation-set.md §5 is about, and it is why a decision run refuses this judge without a --mode=judge-bias artefact. Recorded as a known confound rather than avoided: the pilot exists to measure discordance so §3's n can be computed, and a judge that reads Korean and English equally well matters more to that number than independence from the baseline does.

independentJudge.rationale: mposition's choice for the first independent judge in docs/ops/tomverse-chat-router-evaluation-set.md §5. It has to be independent of both arms, and anthropic/claude-fable-5 wrote neither: the baseline arm is openai/gpt-5.6-luna and the Auto arm is deepseek. Pre-registered here rather than typed at dispatch for the same reason the judge and the seed are -- the calibration compares this judge against the target, and choosing which one after seeing a shift is choosing the answer. It is the expensive half of the measurement at $10/$50 per million tokens against luna's $0.20/$1.20; docs/ops/tomverse-chat-router-calibration-cost.md costs it out.

seed.rationale: mposition's choice. The seed draws the per-item arm ordering, so it decides which answer the judge reads first and position bias is real. Fixed before the run so this is one run rather than the best of several.

notes: A drafted pool that a person has since read. Every item was drafted by a
model, which is what §8 of docs/ops/tomverse-chat-router-evaluation-set.md
allows an agent to produce -- a model-drafted question measures how well a
model handles its own phrasing, so adoption is a human act and is recorded
per item. mposition adopted 210 of them on 2026-08-26, 14 per cell, sheet by
sheet. The remaining 24 stay candidate: they are the reserve a rejected item
would be replaced from, not part of the pilot sample.
Its purpose is to exercise every cell in §2 so the harness can be run and the
pilot discordance measured. lib/routerQualityEvalSet.ts refuses to let it be
used as a decision set.
cellTargets is the §11 freeze record and now holds 14 for each of the 15
cells, entered by mposition. proposedPilotCellTarget still reads 14 and is
kept as the agent proposal the person weighed; the two fields stay separate
because they answer different questions, and agreeing this time does not make
either one the other. 210 is the floor §3's
"200-item pilot" implies once cells are counted separately -- 14 ADOPTED per
cell, so a rejected draft is replaced under a new id rather than counted, and
the number of drafts written exceeded 210.
The baseline is pre-registered rather than chosen after the fact: gpt-5-6-luna
is what every request routes to today, so it is what Auto has to beat.
catalogueVersion pins the commit the model catalogue was read at.
The first 24 items predate the per-item provenance schema. Their drafter was
not recorded at the time and is not reconstructable, so they carry
provider "unrecorded": a guessed drafter would look checkable and would not
be. They are marked so a reviewer can weigh them differently, or reject them
for that reason alone.
frozenDigest is sha256 over what the 210 adopted items ask -- id, cell,
language, prompt, attachment shape, web-search flag -- sorted by id. The
reserve items and these notes are outside it on purpose: this file has to
stay editable after the freeze, so "frozen" had to mean something a later
run can test rather than something the file asserts about itself. A pilot
run recomputes it and refuses if it moved.
pilotReady is true as of the freeze: mposition declaring the pool finished,
which is what turns a short cell from work in progress into an error. It is
not permission to run. purpose stays "development", so --mode=decision still
refuses this file outright, and the cost approval, the judge model and the
seed are all still outstanding.
judge and seed are pre-registered beside the baseline, and the runner now
refuses a run whose --baseline, --judge or --seed disagrees with them. They
were free arguments before, while the report copied these pre-registration
fields in beside whatever was passed: a record could name a person and a
date for a choice they never made.
